tagline: Hill farms, honor-system tables and a bridge planted with flowers.
intro: Route 112 comes over the Vermont line into Colrain and follows the North River down to Shelburne Falls, then runs south through Buckland, Ashfield, Goshen, Cummington and Worthington to Huntington, where the branches of the Westfield River meet. Working farms line it, growing apples, berries, squash, pumpkins, Christmas trees and maple syrup, and some sell from unmarked roadside tables run on the honor system.
The road has moved around. In 1930 it took another line between Worthington and Cummington and stopped at the Mohawk Trail, and it reached Vermont only in 1939, on what had been Route 56.

moments.title: Colrain
moments.text: In May 1812 Colrain became the first town in the country to fly the flag over a public schoolhouse, up in the hilltop village of Catamount.

moments.title: Bridge of Flowers
moments.text: The 1908 trolley bridge could not be torn down because it carried the water main, so in 1929 Shelburne Falls turned it into a garden.

moments.title: William Cullen Bryant Homestead
moments.text: Young Bryant walked seven miles from this hillside house to his law office in Plainfield, and a single bird seen on one of those walks became To a Waterfowl.
